| rf_ask_plain | The site's instructions to automated visitors, and the matching tags carried on the data page. |
| rf_fail | It records one of three things, named in the result: the robots.txt disallows a listed name (for five of the eight names that is a request not to use content for training, not a block on reading); the page's meta tags restrict it; or no robots.txt is served at all, which declares no restriction and under the standard permits every crawler. A fail is therefore not a finding that the agency declared a policy restricting crawler access, and it is about declared policy only, not about whether any crawler is actually served or refused. |
| rf_hypothesis | What does the host declare about crawler access to the data page, in both places a declaration can live (robots.txt and the page's robots meta tag)? A declaration is the publisher's stated policy; it is half of the question whether crawlers are let in, and the half that can be read from outside. |
| rf_name_brief | What the site states about automated access |
| rf_not_measured | The declared layer could not be looked at, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client; the client's own robots.txt compliance kept it from reading the page; or it could not confirm an absence, or a server or network error stopped it. |
| rf_partial | This is a declaration that is read but not scored, so no partial result is given. |
| rf_pass | This records what the agency declares; it is read but not scored. What it records as permitting: both the robots.txt and the page's meta tags, as written, allow each of the eight listed crawler names. |
| rf_question | What does the host say in writing about letting crawlers reach the data page, in both places such a statement can live — the site's robots.txt file and the page's robots meta tags? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "rfc-9309-robots-exclusion-protocol", "quote": "then the crawler MAY access any resources on the server."}, {"source": "https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag", "quote": "rule applies to search engine crawlers"}, {"source": "openai-crawlers-bots", "quote": "Disallowing GPTBot indicates a site's content should not be used in training generative AI foundation models."}, {"source": "rfc-9309-robots-exclusion-protocol", "quote": "These rules are not a form of access authorization."}, {"source": "https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag", "quote": "these settings can be read and followed only if crawlers are allowed to access the pages that include these settings"}, {"source": "openai-crawlers-bots", "quote": "To help ensure your site appears in search results, we recommend allowing OAI-SearchBot in your site's robots.txt file"}, {"source": "anthropic-crawler-support-article", "quote": "it signals that the site's future materials should be excluded from our AI model training"}, {"source": "cloudflare-ai-crawl-control-manage-crawlers", "quote": "For each AI crawler, you can choose to allow or block access."}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |

| rf_state | invalid |
| rf_tells_plain | What the agency has put in writing about which automated visitors may read the page. |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client asks for the robots.txt file and reads the data page's robots meta tags, then checks what each says about the same eight listed crawler names. |
| rf_where_we_look | At the site's robots.txt file and at the robots meta tags carried on the data page. |
| rf_who_else | No public tool runs this exact check. |
| rf_why_it_matters | An RFC on robots.txt defines the file and states plainly that its rules are not a form of access authorization, and Google's crawler documentation defines the robots meta tag and notes those settings can be followed only if crawlers are allowed to read the pages that carry them. This is a declaration: it records what the agency states, read but not scored. |
| rf_why_short | The internet standard for that instructions file says it is not a lock; this records a statement and is not scored. |

| signal | The DECLARED layer only: robots.txt and meta-robots directives for the product path. The enforced and observed layers need edge/WAF logs and are agency_instrumented. |
